Special Council Meeting CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL

WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 20, 2008
06:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 at least 48 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24.
A full City Council agenda packet with all backup information is available at City Hall and the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library the Friday before each Council meeting and on the web at www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents that are regarding an agenda item and received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour and 30 minutes prior to the meeting on the meeting day will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

Special Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
Special Council Meeting
Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority
MINUTES
JOINT SPECIAL MEETING
Wednesday, August 20, 2008
06:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS 635 S. HIGHWAY 101,
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
AND
Teleconference Location (Councilmember Campbell)
15 Brindle Avenue, Dennysport, Massachusetts, 02369
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Mayor Roberts called for the roll call.
Angela Ivey, City Clerk, announced that all Council was present with Councilmember Campbell present via teleconference.
Present:
Roberts, Nichols, Campbell, Heebner, and Kellejian.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Johanna N. Canlas, City Attorney
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Wende Protzman, Dir. Admin. Services/Deputy City Mgr
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director
Tina Christiansen, Comm. Dev. Dir.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer
FLAG SALUTE:
Pete Cohen led the flag salute.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Nichols.
Motion carried unanimously.
STAFF REPORTS:
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk.
A.1.
November 2008 General Municipal Election - Consideration of Facts. (File 0430-20)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Review the Certification of Facts and choose one of two options:
a.
Adopt Resolution 2008-150 appointing nominees to elected offices.
OR
b.
Elect to hold the November 4, 2008 General Municipal Election as planned.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Pete Cohen thanked Council for their service and encouraged Council to forgo the election and save the funds.
Mary Jane Boyd thanked Council for their service that the process supports the best candidates and provides their positions to the public, that there are three good candidates for the three positions and support the Council deciding to forgo the election which would save time, that she believed that citizens are satisfied with the current Council, and that the only disadvantage the cancellation of an election would have is the disallowing of an opportunity for write-in candidates but that with three incumbants would make a write-in candidate potential difficult.
Jack Hegenauer said that he supported certifying the nominees rather than having an election. He said he considered running when he thought there may not be three candidates, that he was satisfied with the current Council and deserve another term, that holding an election would achieve a neutral position and a waste of funds and therefore a meaningless election.
Julie Ustin stated that she supported a decision to forgo the election since there was no opposition.
Marion Dodson said that she supported forgoing the election to save funds and time.
Deputy Mayor Nichols said he had heard the same sentiment in the community.
Councilmember Campbell said his only concern was eliminating the option for a write-in candidate.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that there had not been a write-in candidate in the history of the City.
Councilmember Kellejian said that there is a direct disadvantage of a write-in candidate and asked staff to verify.
Angela Ivey, City Clerk, stated that a write-in candidate does not receive a candidate statement and their name would not be listed on the ballot.
Councilmember Kellejian asked if there are any other disadvantages.
Angela Ivey, City Clerk, said that the only other thing that comes to mind that the candidate would have to educate the community of their candidacy during a shorter time period than candidates that were declared beforehand.
Deputy Mayor Nichols asked staff to review what notification is done to alert the community of open positions.
Angela Ivey, City Clerk, stated that when elections approach the information is posted on the website and bulletin board, that there are calls received throughout the year, that it was not the practice of the City to activey advertise but consistently noticed appropriately by publishing as required in four languages.
Councilmember Heebner appreciated the process, the notification of the meeting tonight, and the speakers that did show and supported the cancellation of the election.
Mayor Roberts said that the public would not want the City to spend the funds and was surprised that was not automatic to cancel elections when there was not any opposition.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Roberts to adopt Resolution 2008-150 appointing nominees, David W. Roberts, Lesa Heebner, and Joe Kellejian, to office of councilmember (commencing on December 10, 2008) and cancelling the Solana Beach General Municipal Election on November 4, 2008 and to remain with the current seating.
Motion carried 4/1
(Noes: Campbell.)
ADJOURN:
Mayor Roberts adjourned the meeting at 6:25 p.m.
